context: SE-AUTOMATION-001F (AUTO-04) implements the EXECUTE → OBSERVE pipeline extension. Two new commands extend the deterministic pipeline: `se execute` (CMD-0022) executes tasks in topological order with authorization, evidence, artifacts, and fail-closed semantics; `se observe` (CMD-0023) provides a read-only observation envelope of execution state. Both produce machine-readable JSON envelopes (`se.execute/1`, `se.observe/1`). The AUTO-04 report originally cited a non-existent ADR-0025; this ADR formally records the architectural decisions for AUTO-04.
problem: How can SYSTEM-ENGINEERING provide deterministic task execution with authorization, evidence collection, artifact creation, and fail-closed semantics, plus a read-only observation envelope, without introducing autonomous execution, LLM routing, or new persistence engines?

options_considered.option: Implement execute/observe as native se_core commands with deterministic envelopes (chosen)
pros: Composes existing gate evaluation, topological planning, and collection functions
Authorization via authorized_actions per task (IMPLEMENT gate)
Read-only observe command enables CI/SE-CONSOLE consumption
No LLM, no autonomous execution, no new engines
cons: Adds two commands (CMD-0022, CMD-0023) requiring adapter regeneration
Requires G3 gate before execution (strict ordering)
Execution receipts add new artifact type

options_considered.option: Extend existing `se implement` with execution semantics

decision: Add two commands to the canonical pipeline: `se execute` (CMD-0022, execution_intent=IMPLEMENT, gate=G3) and `se observe` (CMD-0023, execution_intent=ANALYZE, no gate). `se execute` runs tasks in topological order, validates authorized_actions includes IMPLEMENT, creates execution evidence (EVD-*.json), deliverable artifacts (ART-*.json), and execution receipts (EXR-*.json). Fails closed on first failure unless --continue-on-error. Supports --dry-run (simulation only), --force (re-execute DONE), --task (single task). `se observe` reads task states, evidence, artifacts, and receipts; emits `se.observe/1` envelope. Both commands are fully deterministic, schema-validated, and produce machine-readable JSON.
reason: The EXECUTE → OBSERVE pair completes the deterministic pipeline (intent → plan → execute → observe) without autonomous behavior. Fail-closed, explicit authorization (IMPLEMENT), and auditable receipts satisfy governance requirements. Read-only observe enables CI and SE-CONSOLE to consume execution state without becoming authoritative. The implementation reuses existing topological planning, gate evaluation, and collection functions — no new engines or stores.
consequences: Positive: 401/401 tests PASS (AUTO-04); adapter regenerated to 23 commands, 43 artifacts, 42 generated files, 42 hashes; idempotent generation; four canonical scenarios verified (G3 FAIL, G3 PASS+unauthorized, G3 PASS+authorized+dry-run, G3 PASS+authorized+real). Negative: COMMANDS/commands.json expanded to 24 commands (CMD-0022, CMD-0023); adapter regenerated; two new schemas (execute.schema.json, observe.schema.json) registered in SCHEMAS/index.json. The AUTO-04 report originally cited ADR-0025; this ADR (0030) supersedes that reference.
